subject: Re: Private VPC / Air-gapped feasibility & competitive follow-up
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>

Subject: Follow-up: Private VPC / Air-gapped feasibility & next steps

Hi Alice — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Summary of needs (from the call)
- Private/VPC deployment or fully air-gapped on-prem option for regulated PHI workloads
- Strong control-plane isolation: preference for customer-managed control plane or a private control plane inside their VPC
- KMS/HSM integration and auditability (customer-managed keys)
- Strict egress restrictions — ideally zero egress for the air-gapped option
- Pilot scope: a small production-like workload (2 models, ~200 req/s peak) to validate latency and operational workflows

Competitive points we discussed
- Hyperscalers (AWS/GCP) often require building significant orchestration and observability; Redwood provides a unified runtime + rollout tooling that reduces ops lift
- For private deployments we offer two paths: (1) Private control plane hosted in a customer VPC (minimal peering/egress) and (2) fully air-gapped on-prem bundle with offline install and support

Immediate next steps
1) Marissa to share the networking diagram and POC runbook (attachments) — target to send by EOD tomorrow
2) Redwood to provide a one-pager comparing our private options vs hyperscalers and a preliminary quote for a 2-week pilot
3) Acme to confirm target nodes/OS and whether a temporary peering/VPN is available for the pilot (or confirm fully air-gapped is required)
4) Schedule POC kickoff: proposed week of July 19 — any preference for date/time?

Attachments: redwood-private-vpc-one-pager.pdf; redwood-soc2-summary.pdf; networking-diagram.png (stubs)

Thanks — I’ve copied Marissa and Aditya to help with the technical details.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz

Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-13T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Private VPC / Air-gapped feasibility & next steps

Hi Alice — thanks, wanted to answer your Qs with more technical detail. See inline below and attached runbook stub.

1) Control plane connectivity
- Private control plane (recommended for many customers): we can deploy a control-plane cluster into your customer VPC (via our deployment package). In that mode the control plane communicates with Redwood's backend only if you opt into centralized telemetry/managed updates. If you choose "no egress," the control plane will not phone home — the managed features that require telemetry will be disabled.
- If you want minimal egress: typical endpoints are telemetry.redwood.com:443 and updates.redwood.com:443 (TLS). We'll provide IP ranges and FQDNs for allowlisting.

2) Air-gapped / on-prem bundle
- Fully offline bundle available as a signed artifact (tar.gz) plus an install helper (containerized). Bundle size depends on selected model artifacts; expect ~2–8GB for runtime + small models, larger if you bring large model weights. Upgrades are supported via offline bundles and a signed patch process; we provide a documented patching cadence and remote support for applying patches in-airgap.

3) KMS / HSM
- We support: AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and customer HSM (PKCS#11) integrations for wrapping DEKs. With HSM integration, key material never leaves your HSM; Redwood stores only wrapped keys. We can provide a technical runbook for an HSM-backed setup (requires a small agents service to talk to the HSM within your network).

4) Audit evidence / SOC2
- Attached: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (brief) and a list of artifacts we commonly provide during vendor reviews (SOC2 summary, penetration test summary, architecture diagrams, dataflow diagrams, logging/audit log samples). If you need a full SOC2 report we can start an NDA + secure transfer.

Networking details (very high level)
- For POC with private control plane via VPC peering / Transit Gateway: allow TLS 443 outbound to the specific IP ranges; SSH only for support if explicitly requested and whitelisted.
- For air-gapped: no external endpoints required; we will need S3-like storage accessible locally for model artifacts and a staging bucket for the install artifacts.

Attachments: acme-networking-runbook-template.pdf; networking-diagram.png; redwood-private-install-guide.zip (install scripts, templates).

POC proposal
- Step 0: share target environment details (OS, container runtime, available hosts, internal DNS, NAT/ePN).
- Step 1: pilot deployment in a private VPC control plane mode (1 control plane cluster + 2 inference nodes)
- Step 2: run latency and throughput tests + a simple failover exercise
- Step 3: optional air-gap migration if you want to prove zero-egress mode

Can you send the environment details (OS, container runtime, outbound policy) and confirm July 19 10:00am PT for kickoff?

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
